newsitem.title: FRANCE: Congo minister rules out talks with ex-president.
newsitem.headline: Congo minister rules out talks with ex-president.

text.p: The foreign minister of the divided African state of Congo said on Tuesday his government would not negotiate with former president Denis Sassou Nguesso, whose followers are locked in battle with government troops.
"Nothing is negotiable," Destin Arsene Tsaty-Mboungou, holder of the foreign affairs portfolio in the government of President Pascal Lissouba, told a news conference.

Tsaty-Mboungou said the only way out of the crisis, which has sparked open warfare in the capital Brazzaville, was outside mediation to create conditions for a planned July 27 presidential election in which the two men could square off peacefully.
Asked what had become of an accord which French President Jacques Chirac's office said had been reached with both sides for a cease-fire, Tsaty-Mboungou replied:
"No. For the time being the fire has not ceased. It continues to kill in Brazzaville but I hope that the appeals for peace which were made will be heard by both sides."
Chirac's spokeswoman Catherine Colonna said on Monday the French leader had received verbal agreement for a cease-fire in telephone conversations with both Lissouba and Sassou-Nguesso.
French officials said both sides were co-operating with French troops in the capital.

France has sent 400 troops to reinforce the 450 already in Brazzaville, where they were sent in March in case foreigners needed to be evacuated from Kinshasa, the neighbouring capital of Laurent Kabila's Congo.
French officials in the Congo said between 700 and 800 foreigners were flown out of Brazzaville on Monday in Transall military transport planes to the Gabon capital Libreville.
They said more than 1,000 French citizens could still be in the Brazzaville area.

When Tsaty-Mboungou was asked if Lissouba would ask for the French troops to step in on the government side, he replied: "It is up to the French authorities to see if they deem it necessary to... help a legitimate government".

French junior minister for Cooperation Charles Josselin said on Monday that Paris saw blame on both sides but Tsaty-Mboungou said he met Josselin on Tuesday and was told France still recognised his government as the legitimate one.
French diplomats meanwhile repeated that the 850 troops Paris sent to Brazzaville would intervene solely to protect or evacuate foreign civilians.

Gunfire rattled through the city for a sixth day on Tuesday in fighting between soldiers and militiamen loyal to Lissouba and a political militia loyal to Sassou Nguesso. French soldiers moved through the city rescuing foreigners trapped by fighting.
